mainEntity.name: Is the 60-hour course the same as the 20-hour course?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The 60-hour course is qualifying education for the entry process. The 20-hour CTEC course is annual continuing education for registered preparers.

mainEntity.name: Can I take the CTEC 60 hour course online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Online options are available. Confirm whether the course is self-paced or scheduled, how lessons and exams work, and whether your preferred device is supported.

mainEntity.name: Do I need tax preparation experience first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Qualifying education covers foundational material. Check the school’s entry requirements and sample lessons to judge whether its pace and explanations suit your starting knowledge.

CTEC’s self-study standards include examination requirements. Ask the provider how assessments are organized, what score is required, and what support or retakes are available. See CTEC’s QE standards .

mainEntity.name: How long do I have to complete the course?

acceptedAnswer.text: The school sets its course-access and completion terms. CTEC separately states that completed qualifying education is valid for up to 18 months from completion. Plan both the course and registration around the applicable dates. See CTEC’s new-application timeframes .

mainEntity.name: Can I prepare tax returns as soon as I finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Completing the course alone does not grant CTEC registration. If you are required to register, complete the remaining application and registration requirements before practicing. CTEC explains the process in its new-preparer instructions .

mainEntity.name: How do I know a provider offers approved qualifying education?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check the school’s current qualifying education approval in the CTEC provider directory . Approval for continuing education alone is not the same as approval for qualifying education.
